item.title: Re: My SCP Idea
item.content:encoded:
Not an official critter.

+ Crit crit
- Tirc tirc

First off, I'm concerned that this skip is too dangerous to be interesting. It's a black hole that sucks in the Sun, and in 200 years the sun will be gone.

SCP-XXXX is an alien object that orbits the sun which sucks 1-5% of it's energy

1-5% is a ridiculous number. That means, in 200 years or more, the Sun will be completely vapori[z|s]ed. Also, wouldn't people notice?

The SCP Foundation would try to reduce the energy intake of the alien base

So, like, how? How would the Foundation send a vessel in High Solar Orbit with enough fuel to spare to rendezvous with the alien base without detection?

The Foundation would have no way to contain the object

Couldn't they just shoot it? This seems more like a job for the GOC than the SCP Foundation who specializes in anomalies. If there were anomalies in the ship, the SCP Foundation could take care of it.

Earth would be stuck in a permanent ice age.

No, all of Earth would be ice and without the Sun it'd probably be sucked into Jupiter or be flung off into space forever.

Overall, this idea is written very vaguely, and seems more dangerous than interesting.

item.title: Re: My SCP Idea
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello! Not an official critter or anyone with any sort of authority, but I can still read and give my thoughts.
And when reading this, they are pretty much two.

One, is that there isn't really… much to this, at all, I feel. It feels very much like a Series I object. Better yet, it feels like a 'thing that does a thing'. Yes, there is this alien object that orbits the sun and sucks up energy. So? Besides this idea probably having already been written, at least to some capacity- I'd have to check as this kind of skip isn't generally my thing- what story do you have to tell?

The central narrative sounds like what you'd expect from any SCP article where the object cannot be contained, aka the Foundation trying to remedy the effects of said object; what sets it apart? Nowadays, at least from what I see, people want more from their SCPs. They want a story. A narrative.

For instance, you could expand on where this alien object comes from; you say it is an 'alien base'. That implies to me there is an alien civilization that built it. Who are they? What do they want? Why did they build this?
If it were me, given this framework, I'd have them build this station because they are running out of energy and will all die if they don't do this. This not only provides a narrative, but also introduces the ethical question for the Foundation of 'do we let them die to save ourselves'?

All in all, I recommend you expand your idea draft! There is potential to this idea, so I think you could get something interesting out of it.
I hope this was helpful in some way!

item.title: My SCP Idea
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is an alien object that orbits the sun which sucks 0.2-3% of it's energy
every decade. The Foundation would try to stop it so Earth doesn't become a frozen hellhole.

Central Narrative: The SCP Foundation would try to reduce the energy intake of the alien base that was sent to the solar system because of an energy crisis with several different ways. The story would take over a span of 35 years with the Foundation enlisting the help of the United Nations to stop the anomalous object.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: If the foundation were to destroy the object, the Alien civilization could die out which brings out the the ethical question for the Foundation of 'do we let them die to save ourselves'?

Additional Notes: I would like assistance on expanding this idea further, and if there's any issues with it, I would appreciate if you would tell me what's wrong with it.
